faq.q: How is a racing car wing like a plane wing?
faq.a: It has the same curved, angled shape as an aircraft wing, but mounted upside down. So the force it makes points down towards the road instead of up into the sky.
asks: Is a car spoiler like an airplane wing?

faq.q: How does a wing push a car down?
faq.a: The wing is angled to turn the air that flows past it upward. Pushing air up pushes the wing down, and the pressure on its top surface becomes higher than underneath.
asks: How does a rear wing work?

faq.a: Downforce is a downward push from air flowing over a car's wings and body. At high speed a Formula 1 car makes more downforce than its own weight, so in theory it could drive upside down on a ceiling.
asks: Could a Formula 1 car drive upside down?

faq.q: Why does more downforce mean more grip?
faq.a: Tyre grip depends on how hard the tyre is pressed onto the road. Downforce presses harder without adding mass that would also have to be sped up and slowed down.

faq.q: Why don't ordinary cars have big wings?
faq.a: At normal road speeds a wing makes very little downforce but still adds drag, which wastes fuel. Big wings only pay off at racing speeds.
asks: Do spoilers on normal cars do anything?

facts: Downforce grows with the square of speed.
At high speed a Formula 1 car can make more downforce than its own weight.
Wings make drag as well as downforce, so racing teams trade cornering grip against straight-line speed.
